ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD/EDD under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and FATF Recommendations 10, 12 and 17: beneficial owners holding 25% or more must be identified before incorporation; applicants are screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, Samoa domestic designation lists issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and Samoa FIU directives; foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international-organization PEPs are subject to enhanced due diligence, senior-management sign-off, source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring; given the USD-linked payment rails (PayPal Mass Payout and Wise), prudent market practice also requires OFAC SDN-list screening. Any sanctions hit or PEP-derived funding flagged at screening must be reported to the Samoa FIU via Suspicious Transaction Report before incorporation proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA Online Registry (e-Registry) of the Samoa International Finance Authority, maintained by the Registrar of International Companies, Apia (https://www.sifa.ws)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in English using Roman/Latin script; Samoan names must also be written in Roman script without compulsory diacritical marks (the koma liliu is permitted but not mandatory); a name is registerable only if it is not identical or visually/phonetically confusingly similar to an existing International Company name, a reserved name, a domestic company name, or a name protected by international convention notified to the Registrar; the name must end with an approved suffix such as Limited, Ltd, Corporation, Corp, Incorporated, Inc, Company, Co, or a permitted Samoan abbreviation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar of International Companies rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar within 14 calendar days, attaching revised name alternatives and any required consents (e.g., Central Bank of Samoa approval for bank/trust/insurance tokens); if the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may appeal to the Minister responsible for the Samoa International Finance Authority within 21 days, and thereafter seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa on procedural or legal grounds. A fresh name reservation may be filed concurrently without prejudice; engagement of Samoan counsel is recommended. No separate public fee is prescribed for the reconsideration step.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this industry. An International Company carrying on a remote market-research SaaS business need not maintain operational premises in Samoa. The International Companies Act 1987 requires a statutory registered office in Samoa at the premises of a licensed International Company service provider (registered agent), which lawfully functions as a virtual office. The IC must not transact business with Samoan residents or hold Samoan land except in the narrowly permitted offshore cases (ss. 60-63 of the 1987 Act). Payment providers (PayPal/Wise) may request a physical-address or substance explanation; the registered-agent arrangement and the IC's offshore exempt-tax status constitute the required statutory substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% ex-ante likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection of the statutory registered office by the Registrar or SIFA supervisors; the Samoan registered agent's licensed premises are subject to risk-based AML/CFT inspections, but the offshore operational site of the IC is not physically inspected by Samoan regulators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (No. 18, 1987), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015; Sections 5-6 (Incorporation), Section 8 (Registered Office), Section 10 (Directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association filed on Form 1, resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation under Section 6 of the International Companies Act 1987
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued with par or no par value, and no escrow account is required. Paid-up capital may remain nil until the board resolves otherwise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) The issue and allotment of the authorized share capital to the charter subscriber(s) is hereby confirmed and accepted. (2) The registered office maintained by the Registered Agent at [Agent Address, Apia, Samoa] is adopted as the Company's statutory registered office under Section 8 of the International Companies Act 1987. (3) [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed as first directors, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each to hold office until removal in accordance with the Articles. (4) The directors are authorized to open bank accounts and engage PayPal and Wise payment channels for the consumer market research platform.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application with a proposed company name ending in 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. Provide a brief statement of business objects. SIFA checks confidentiality and misleading-name criteria before reserve endorsement.
required_dossiers: Brief business purpose description and ISIC 7320 activity declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, resubmit the application with an alternative name within 5 business days; if rejected again, appeal to SIFA with supporting evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutive Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Notary Public / Licensed International Company Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English. Have all subscriber(s) execute the documents before a notary public. The licensed agent certifies copies and prepares the Statement of Compliance for registration.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (original and certified copy)
Consent to act as Director and Secretary
Certification of compliance by authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or agent identifies defects, correct the drafting deficiencies and re-execute the documents within 24 hours; the SIFA online submission will not accept improperly executed documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Form 1 through the SIFA online platform or counter submission, attaching the certified Memorandum and Articles, registered office consent, agent certification, and proof of advance payment of the USD 150 incorporation fee.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Letter of Consent from Registered Agent to maintain registered office
Certificate of compliance to be registered
Proof of payment of government filing fee (USD 150)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a query or requisition, provide the requested clarifications or corrected filings within 7 days; if the application is rejected, file a sworn explanation and re-apply with amended documents or appeal to the Minister of Commerce within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance and Statutory Register Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent, SIFA; First Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, hold an initial board meeting; adopt the first board resolution; issue subscribed share certificates; and set up the registered office and statutory books at the filed address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records are incomplete or the first board resolution is not adopted, convene a corrective board meeting within 7 days; late or defective register filings may attract a monthly penalty of USD 10 per document, cured by submission of revised records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable (no physical industrial establishment; office-based SaaS market research platform)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no operational license required for consumer polling and data analytics under Samoan law)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) – Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category 5: Non-physical commercial service, no land use modification)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge; ordinary office waste is collected under Solid Waste Management Regulations 2017; any e-waste disposal must comply with the Samoa E-Waste Management Regulations 2020.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for virtual operations. For the physical registered office (agent's licensed office), a Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority is required to guarantee compliance with the National Fire Safety standard; workplace injury coverage is confirmed through the Samoa Accident Compensation Corporation (SACC) registration for the nominal staff count.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa (Inland Revenue Department and Samoa Customs Service), electronic services portal: Talamo e-Filing (www.revenue.gov.ws); overseas entity registry and International Company supervisor: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA, www.sifa.ws) acting under the International Companies Act 1987 and the International Companies Regulation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: International Companies do not require a Ministry for Revenue TIN for offshore business. Procedure: (1) engage a SIFA-licensed registered agent and file the Articles of Incorporation; (2) SIFA issues the Certificate of Incorporation, the IC registration number and the statutory tax-exemption status certificate; this certificate constitutes the entity's tax identity for banks and investors; (3) obtain a TIN and/or GST registration from the Ministry for Revenue only if the IC opens a local Samoa bank account, becomes a GST registrant for domestic taxable supplies, or must act as a Samoa withholding agent — application is made by the registered agent on the prescribed MfR form, attaching the SIFA certificate, constitution, directors, and registered-office confirmation; (4) turnaround: SIFA certificate within 1 business day; supplementary MfR TIN within 3–5 business days; (5) no minimum capital and no non-resident ownership restriction apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — Samoa IC is statutorily exempt non-resident: no Samoa corporate income tax, dividend withholding tax, GST, capital gains tax, customs import duty or stamp duty on qualifying offshore business; exemption is automatic and not elective, conditional on the statutory restrictions (no business with Samoan residents, no Samoan land interests, no management and control in Samoa, no Samoa-source income, licensed registered agent maintained).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Samoan check-the-box election: the IC is an opaque corporation by law. (1) Domestic conversion: an IC may elect, by special resolution with SIFA consent, to register as an ordinary Samoa domestic company and thereby become subject to entity-level taxation under the Income Tax Act 2015 — an opt-in into the taxable regime. (2) Foreign-company downgrade: the IC may elect to be struck from the IC register and re-licensed as a foreign company branch, giving rise to Samoan tax only on Samoa-source income. (3) Hybrid-mismatch rules: Samoa does not provide a hybrid election; the IC's tax status is determined by the investor jurisdiction's classification rules (e.g., US check-the-box, CFC regimes, OECD Pillar Two income-inclusion rule), and the 2015 Income Tax Act contains CFC and general anti-avoidance rules relevant only to Samoan-resident shareholders.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — Samoa's broad-based value-added tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992 (as amended).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 50,000 (Samoan Tala) of annual taxable supplies measured on a 12-month (rolling or prospective) basis; mandatory GST registration applies when the threshold is met or exceeded; voluntary registration is open to suppliers of taxable supplies; a Samoa International Company whose supplies are zero-rated offshore international services is outside the registration net but may optionally register to recover GST on Samoan inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate applies: Samoa does not operate an e-invoicing clearance/API system, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls. GST-registered suppliers may issue paper or PDF tax invoices with the prescribed GST particulars; GST returns are filed electronically on the Ministry for Revenue's Talamo e-Services portal, and customs export declarations are transmitted through ASYCUDA World. Cross-border SaaS invoices issued by the Consumer Panel Survey Platform to overseas clients in PDF/email format, without XML clearance or fiscal codes, are legally sufficient.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: zero-rated when actually exported from Samoa and supported by customs documentation and foreign payment. Services: zero-rated as 'international services' when the recipient is a non-resident located outside Samoa at the time of supply, the service is not physically performed in Samoa to a material extent, and it does not relate to Samoan land or goods in Samoa. The Consumer Panel Survey Platform's electronic market-research SaaS qualifies for zero-rating on the offshore platform fee; any on-the-ground consumer polling fieldwork actually performed in Samoa is a local taxable supply (15% GST) and should be separately invoiced. An IC operating wholly offshore does not charge GST; if voluntarily GST-registered, it may zero-rate the SaaS export and obtain refunds of input GST on Samoan overheads.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via ASYCUDA World (Samoa Customs Service)
Commercial invoice bearing the supplier's GST registration number and zero-rated endorsement
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of goods from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of foreign exchange within the statutory repatriation window
For pure digital/international services: recipient tax-residence certificate, service agreement and online-delivery records replace the customs documents
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Audit scrutiny is dual: the Ministry for Revenue (with Samoa Customs) audits GST, income and export substantiation; SIFA audits IC exemption compliance under the International Companies Act 1987. Enforced corrective measures for false zero-rating claims and misuse of IC exemptions: (1) GST shortfall assessment reversed to 15% plus additional tax (25% late-payment tax and 2% per month/marginal penalty tax under the GST Act), monetary fines and imprisonment on conviction; (2) shortfall penalties up to 150% for deliberate tax evasion under the Tax Administration Act 2012, with the Commissioner able to disregard anti-avoidance arrangements and to assess for up to 8 years in fraud cases; (3) an IC that breaches its statutory exemption conditions becomes retrospectively assessable on Samoan-source income at ordinary rates, may be struck off by SIFA, and incurs SIFA administrative fines; (4) zero-rated export claims not substantiated within the documentation window are clawed back with interest running from the original GST due date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia, Samoa
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates under the Exchange Control Act and CBS Exchange Control Regulations, preserving current account convertibility for trade and services, while capital account transactions remain subject to approval thresholds. Non-resident controlled International Companies (ICs) may maintain foreign-currency and WST tala accounts through licensed commercial banks, and profits or proceeds derived from offshore business may be remitted freely provided source documentation and bank compliance validation are satisfactory. There are no domestic tax-clearance hurdles for ICs because the entity enjoys zero corporate income tax in Samoa, but transaction reason codes and beneficial ownership disclosures must be furnished.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa's exchange control framework requires Samoan resident exporters to repatriate export proceeds to Samoa through a licensed CBS bank within the statutory ninety-day period and to convert export receipts to WST tala except where CBS has granted an exemption. For a non-resident-owned International Company relying on the International Companies Act exemptions, mandatory surrender does not apply automatically; clean offshore collections into foreign-currency accounts are permitted, but any inward payment intended for local WST use must be supported by an exchange control application and, where required, a written exemption obtained by the licensed bank before conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited (BSP Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for survey-panel collections and mass payouts
Capital Escrow Account for inbound shareholder capital injection
Operational WST tala account for local vendor and regulatory payments
Secondary foreign-currency clearing account for USD and AUD settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM. PayPal and Wise are not licensed banks in Samoa and cannot independently provide Samoa IBANs or clear WST tala. They are treated as cross-border payment aggregators and can be used for consumer-panel mass payouts only if paired with a licensed Samoan bank or with duly authorised money remittance operators under the Money Remittance Act 2016. Use of offshore EMIs is legally permissible for settling commercial obligations outside Samoa, but they do not satisfy CBS prudential banking or AML/CFT onboarding for treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Rules and the Money Laundering Prevention Act require licensed banks to establish the true identity and beneficial ownership of corporate clients. Although Samoa permits a registered agent to submit the corporate opening package, at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner must normally attend an in-person interview at the bank branch in Apia or at a CBS-accredited foreign branch in a recognised correspondent jurisdiction. Remote video KYC is possible for low-risk customers only with an enhanced approval by the bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer and with a Samoa registered agent physically certifying the original constitutional documents; however, first-time IC account opening predominantly requires physical presence of a signatory director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company with no commercial footprint in Samoa and no independent office registration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Incorporation Certificate, certified Memorandum and Articles of Association, Certificate of Good Standing, Registered Agent Certificate proving registered office in Samoa, board resolution appointing signatories, written business plan describing the survey-platform operating model, and an executed declaration identifying all natural-person ultimate beneficial owners with source-of-funds statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border consumer-panel mass payouts creating many small-value beneficiary credits in multiple countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction monitoring policy, panelist risk-tiering matrix, automated sanctions and PEP screening, panelist KYC or pseudonym-contract mapping, anti-fraud and duplicate-claim detection controls, evidence of data-subject consent under applicable privacy law, and a batch-payout file format approved by the bank to enable review of payee jurisdictions and payment justification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chinese or other high-risk jurisdictional Chinese beneficial owner without physical Samoa residence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and residence permit certified by a notary or Samoa-registered agent, independent address verification utility bill within six months, economic-beneficiary declaration, source-of-wealth documents comprising audited financial statements or bank references, professional reference letters, and a clear explanation of the ownership chain from the Chinese individual to the Samoa International Company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual projected transaction velocity for a newly registered low-risk survey platform, including large monthly aggregate settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A bank-level MLRO underwriting file containing projected monthly inflows and outflows, administrative expense projections, panelist count and average payout value, a funds-flow diagram from clients to the Samoa IC and onward to international panelists, sub-processor contracts with payment aggregators, and a commitment to provide quarterly bank statements and transaction-level audit trails upon request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection is routed by SWIFT MT103 from the parent shareholder's account to the Samoa IC's foreign-currency capital escrow account at ANZ Bank (Samoa) Limited, with CBS-approved remittance purpose code /SUBS/ or 'Equity capital and shares' and explicit reference to the International Company's registration number. The bank verifies the remitter against the board-approved share subscription list, the registered agent's UBO declaration, and the signed source-of-funds questionnaire; where the amount exceeds CBS exchange-control notification thresholds, a CBS capital import form or exchange-control exemption must be endorsed before the amount is released for operating use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The principal clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for high-value single vendor or contractor payments, SWIFT MT101 for multi-payment batches through the bank's corporate interface, and the domestic Samoan Interbank Settlement System (SISS) for any WST tala local payments. For consumer panel payouts, the platform relies on licensed aggregator APIs, namely PayPal Mass Payout and Wise Business, using a segregated sub-account funded by an outward transfer from the Samoa operating account; commercial letters of credit are not required for the data-research services except where a client demands documentary settlement for a high-value market-research contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CBS-approved spot foreign exchange transactions between WST, USD, AUD and NZD using licensed commercial banks
Short-term deliverable forward contracts of up to twelve months with licensed banks for committed survey-platform trade receipts and payouts
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD executed through an approved international counterparty, with CBS notification where settlement references a Samoan underlying exposure

Currency swaps and structured hedging instruments are permissible only on a case-by-case basis with prior CBS exchange-control approval and are generally impractical in the Samoan offshore banking market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual international company license renewal fee (no separate annual return form is required for a Samoa International Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on each anniversary of incorporation; the annual fee is payable in advance and there is no fixed calendar-year filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee is triggered if the fee remains unpaid after the due date; continued non-payment for 90 days permits the Registrar to publish a strike-off notice, strike the company off the International Companies Register, and dissolve it, with the company's assets vesting in the State.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership and statutory register annual KYC refresh (confirmation of shareholding transfers and current UBO details)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent on behalf of the Registrar of International Companies and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once each calendar year on or before the anniversary of incorporation, and within 14 days of any share transfer, change in directors, or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update beneficial ownership records may result in monetary penalties under Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Act; persistent non-compliance can lead to registered-agent resignation, regulatory sanction, and eventual strike-off of the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a Samoa International Company solely by reason of its corporate status. An audit is required only if the directors voluntarily commission one, if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights requisition an audit, or if an external lender, investor, or foreign regulator requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board; a Samoa International Company must maintain sufficient accounting records to explain transactions and financial position, but is not required to file financial statements with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a beneficial ownership register at its registered office in Samoa. The registered agent must conduct an annual KYC/UBO refresh, verify any shareholding transfers, and record resulting ownership changes in the register. No public UBO filing is made, but the register must be produced to the Registrar, SIFSA, or the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit on lawful request. Non-compliance subjects the company and its registered agent to fines, sanctions, and potential deregistration.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (International Companies are wholly exempt from Samoan Income Tax under the International Companies Act 1988)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption for International Companies; no capital gains tax, dividend withholding tax, or payroll tax; qualifying entities may apply for a tax exemption certificate under the Tax Exemption Act 2017

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (ICAR-001) filed electronically via the Samoa Financial Supervisory Authority (SFSAS) e-Registry portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six (6) months after the company's registration anniversary date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List the licensed Samoan registered agent; this is mandatory and cannot be left blank for foreign-owned entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders Schedule (name, address, nationality, shareholding percentage)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are permitted; provide beneficial owner details and evidence of source of funds where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors Schedule (name, address, nationality, appointment date)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; at least one director is required and may be a natural person.
Confirm that the company has not carried on any Samoan-source business; if it has carried on business in Samoa, it must elect to be taxed as a resident company and lose the IC exemption.
State the fee amount paid through the SFSAS portal; keep proof of payment for audit trail.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a penalty of WST 50 per month or part thereof, plus administrative reinstatement fees; continued default may result in striking-off the International Companies Register and forfeiture of limited liability protection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders (International Companies Act 1988); domestic resident companies are subject to 15% withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2015
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: While an exempt International Company is not subject to Samoan WHT, if a shareholder requires treaty validation, the following protocol applies: (i) request Samoa Tax Certificate of Residence from the Ministry of Revenue; (ii) submit Form WHT-T1 (Treaty Relief Election) for each dividend payment; (iii) provide the tax residence certificate (TRC) of the shareholder from its home jurisdiction; and (iv) retain a Beneficial Ownership Declaration, especially where payments pass through intermediaries.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 15% withholding tax on royalties and 15% on interest paid to non-residents. Under Samoa's double tax agreements, rates may be reduced to 0%–10% on interest and 5%–10% on royalties, contingent on TRC submission and beneficial ownership compliance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory Local File/Master File threshold applies to International Companies because they are exempt from income tax; for taxable resident companies, contemporaneous documentation is required where related-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000 (Local File) or WST 5,000,000 (Master File) per annum.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies Act 1988, as amended by the Economic Substance Regulations 2020, requires every International Company carrying on relevant activities including intellectual property, headquarters, distribution, and service functions to demonstrate economic substance in Samoa or a comparable OECD jurisdiction. A consumer panel survey platform cannot be a mere shell; it must maintain local physical presence, employees, expenditure, and management decision-making for the exempt status to hold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Sham Offshore Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an International Company with no economic substance, concealing Samoan-source income, or receiving cross-border payments while engaging in circular invoicing to mischaracterize service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoa Tax Administration Act 2015, penalties of up to WST 1,000,000 or 150% of the evaded tax, and imprisonment for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, interest, and penalties; courts may pierce the corporate veil, impose travel bans, and freeze personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the International Company as a mailbox entity without any real operations while shifting profits earned from online consumer panel and market research activities to related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off from the International Companies Register, retroactive cancellation of exempt status, fines up to WST 250,000 for false declarations, and possible deemed incorporation as a taxable resident company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for all debts of the company, including tax liabilities, and can face civil restitution orders and disqualification from acting as directors for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cross-border consumer panellist payouts through PayPal Mass Payout or Wise without performing beneficial ownership verification, sanctions screening, or filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoa Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018, entities face fines up to WST 1,000,000, cancellation of money services provider approval, and mandatory compliance audits; individuals are subject to imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, travel bans, confiscation of illegal proceeds, and bans on managing any financial or commercial entity in Samoa.
